name: Jellyfin Federation
description: Aggregate content from multiple Jellyfin servers into unified virtual libraries
overview: The Jellyfin Federation Plugin allows you to create a unified media library by aggregating content from multiple remote Jellyfin servers. Stream content from any server without file synchronization.
changelog:
Fixed the real cause of federated playback taking minutes to start: on a server reached through a public reverse proxy, VPS, or tunnel (the normal setup for most installs), a Proxy-mode stream's URL pointed at that public hostname - so this server's own transcoder round-tripped every byte of the source file back out through DNS/the tunnel just to reach itself. This hit every server with a ServerUrl configured, which peer handshakes require - effectively everyone running Proxy mode. Proxy-mode stream URLs now always resolve to loopback (127.0.0.1) instead, for both the primary source and any alternate multi-server sources, since they are only ever fetched by the local ffmpeg process and never by a client directly. The previous 0.0.64 fix (AnalyzeDurationMs on the federated MediaSourceInfo, intended to shrink ffmpeg's probe) has been removed - live logs confirmed it had no effect on the actual ffmpeg invocation in this Jellyfin version.

Recolored the corner "federated source" badge on grid/list cards from a theme-accent-colored circle to a neutral dark chip. The accent color made it visually indistinguishable from Jellyfin's own theme-accent played-checkmark badge; the dark chip stays legible over any poster art without being mistaken for a native state badge.

198 tests.
